senses.gloss: ch. same, to prolong, let hang down; to let down.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 38:6">Targ. Jer. XXXVIII, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 38:11">11</cite>.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 147b:7">Sabb. 147ᵇ</cite> <he>כי מעבריתו … שַׁרְבִּיבוּ להו וכ׳</he> when you have to carry garments for the soldiers (on the Sabbath), let them hang down over your shoulders (so as to serve as garments for yourselves).

<cite ref="Eruvin 102b:3">Erub. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>שַׁרְבֵּיב בגלימיה טפח</he> (not <he>בגלימי</he>; ed. Sonc. <he>אישתרבב בגלימיה</he>, read: <he>א׳ גלימיה</he>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 200) if a person lets his cloak trail one handbreadth.

<cite ref="Sotah 12b">Sot. 12ᵇ</cite> [read:] <he>אִישְׁתַּרְבְּבָא אִישְׁתַּרְבּוּבֵי</he> (her arm) was prolonged (by a miracle, so that she could reach the infant Moses); <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1">Ex. R. s. 1<sup>23</sup></cite> <he>אישתרבובי אִשְׁתַּרְבּוּב</he> they (her arms) were prolonged; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 166:7">Yalk. ib. 166</cite> <he>אישתרבב אישתרבו</he> (corr. acc.).

senses.gloss: to be let down; to trail; to spread.
units: <cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 7:3">Targ. II Chr. VII, 3</cite>; <cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 7:10">10</cite>.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 24a:16">Snh. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>לבבל נחית ואישתרבובי דאי׳ לעילם</he> it (the measure of pride) came down to Babylonia, but was dragged along to Elam; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 573">Yalk. Zech. 573</cite> <he>ואי׳ להתם</he>.
<cite ref="Beitzah 11a:3">Bets. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>אשתרבובי אשתרבוב ונחות</he> they (the pigeons in the upper nest) dragged themselves along and came down (to the lower nest).
